text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging @Priya (oncall) — severity: high — customer 'Orchid' experiencing tail latency spikes and streaming stalls on single-tenant pool orchid-prod-01. Automated alert: p99 breach (SLO) and stream stall rate > 3%.

Priya: Got the page, joining. What metrics do we have?

Liam: p95 jumped from ~120ms -> ~850ms over the last 10m, p99 peaked at ~2.4s. Streaming stall alerts show partial responses where the stream freezes mid-token for 2–6s.

Jenna: infra-side, I see a node group in the dedicated pool showing high write latency to NVMe and occasional worker restarts (OOM killers not triggered). No obvious autoscaler events.

Marco: Runtime traces show repeated KV-cache miss churn for long-prefix requests. Customer prompt patterns include very long delimiter sequences and repeated prefix tokens — looks like the multiplexer is creating many unique cache keys.

Orchid-CS: We pushed a new prompt pattern yesterday for their summarization batch job — lots of repeated "<<<BATCH>>><<<BATCH>>>" markers. They reported some user-facing slowdowns ~09:12 UTC.

Priya: ok. Quick mitigation brainstorm: 1) route Orchid traffic to fallback model variant with lower cache sensitivity, 2) enable request-shaping (throttle or connection queue) for their tenant, 3) restart a subset of workers on the affected nodegroup after draining. Which is fastest?

Marco: Fastest is routing to a compatible variant we have pre-warmed: model-id: rwd-small-quant-v2. It sacrifices a bit of quality but reduces KV-cache footprint. I can flip routing policy for that tenant.

Jenna: I'll prepare a rolling drain+restart for the hot nodes but will wait until routing is live to reduce customer disruption.

Priya: Marco, do the route swap (canary first, 10% -> 100% in 5m) and keep streaming enabled so we can compare. Post the command you run.

Marco: Executing routing change now.

Marco: Command used:

```
POST https://control-plane.internal/v1/routing/tenants/orchid
Authorization: Bearer <svc-token>
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "target_policy": "fallback-variant",
  "canary": true,
  "canary_ratio": 0.10,
  "reason": "mitigate KV-cache thrash from long-delimiter prompts"
}
```

Marco: Canary live at 09:26:14 UTC. Monitoring p95/p99 for that slice.

Liam: Canary metrics: p95 down from 820ms -> 190ms on the canary slice, p99 down to 420ms. Streaming stall rate on canary 0.6%. Looks good.

Marco: Rolling to 100% now.

incident-bot: Routing update: tenant orchid set to policy fallback-variant (100%) by Marco at 09:29:03 UTC.

Priya: Good. Jenna, you can proceed with a rolling restart of the two most impacted nodes after drain.

Jenna: Draining node n-az3-17 now. Will cordon, drain, restart runtime, then uncordon. Command log:

```
kubectl cordon n-az3-17
kubectl drain n-az3-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m
ssh root@n-az3-17 'systemctl restart redwood-runtime'
kubectl uncordon n-az3-17
```

Jenna: Node back in service at 09:42:57 UTC. Second node restart scheduled in 2m.

Priya: Monitoring after full routing + restarts. Current global numbers: p95 ~150ms, p99 ~450ms, streaming stalls ~0.8% (baseline pre-incident ~0.4%). Customer impact window ~09:12–09:32 UTC. Orchid reports reduced errors, CS confirms degraded quality but acceptable for now.

Orchid-CS: Thanks team. Our support contacts seeing fewer complaints. We'll send a note explaining we temporarily routed to fallback variant.

Priya: Immediate mitigations complete. Handoff for post-incident follow-ups:
- Marco: root-cause follow-up to analyze KV-key cardinality and multiplexer behavior for long-delimiter prompts (ticket RDW-2781).
- Jenna: investigate NVMe write latency anomaly and correlate with system logs (RDW-2782).
- Liam: add a tenant-level protective throttle + autoscaling recommendation for dedicated pools (RDW-2783).
- Marco+Priya: assess whether we can add prompt-normalization rules at the front door to collapse delimiter sequences (RDW-2784).

Priya: Handoff notes for next oncall (Robin):
- What happened: Orchid's unique prompt pattern caused high KV-cache key cardinality -> cache thrash -> higher per-request latency and streaming stalls.
- What we did: applied tenant routing to fallback model (canary -> 100%), restarted two hot nodes, monitored metrics.
- Customer impact: ~20% of Orchid requests in the 09:12–09:32 window experienced >1s latency or streaming stalls; no data loss.
- Current state: service stable for Orchid and global SLOs recovered.
- Follow-ups assigned (see tickets above).

Robin: Taking over. I'll keep the alert closed and watch dashboards for the next 3 hours. Reopen if p99 > 1s or stream stall rate > 2% for orchid.

Priya: Thanks everyone. I'll file the incident writeup and link these notes (RDW-INC-2026).

Marco: Quick data dump we used for analysis:
```
# metric query (internal)
SELECT
  window_start,
  p95_latency_ms,
  p99_latency_ms,
  streaming_stall_rate
FROM tenant_metrics
WHERE tenant_id = 'orchid' AND window_start > '2026-03-15T09:00:00Z'
ORDER BY window_start ASC
```

Liam: Logs we saw on the runtime (excerpt):
```
[09:14:57] runtime: multiplexer: new-cache-key: prefix=<<<<<BATCH>>>>> len=512 hash=0x9a3f
[09:15:01] runtime: kvcache: miss thrash count=1247
[09:15:05] runtime: stream: stall detected: last_output_delta=4230ms conn=orchid-conn-42
[09:15:10] kernel: nvme0n1: write latency spike 18ms -> 210ms
```

Priya: Good. We'll include these logs in the writeup. Closing thread once writeup is posted. :white_check_mark:
